readerTitle: Circuit City in 2008: the shop that ran out of credit before it ran out of customers
caseNote: 실제 기업·사건 (Circuit City, Lehman Brothers, Best Buy, 2008 금융위기) + 가상 적용 (인력 파견 회사)
insight: 금융위기는 수요보다 먼저 신용을 끊는다. 위기에서 살아남는 회사를 가르는 것은 이익률이 아니라 '남의 돈 없이 몇 주를 버틸 수 있는가'다.
misconception: 불황에 회사가 망하는 이유는 손님이 줄어서다. 매출만 지키면 버틸 수 있다.

sources.text: Circuit City press release on its Chapter 11 filing, November 10, 2008 (cites vendors tightening credit terms)
Circuit City press release announcing liquidation, January 16, 2009
Lehman Brothers Holdings Chapter 11 filing, September 15, 2008 (U.S. Bankruptcy Court, S.D.N.Y.)

Sequoia Capital, 'R.I.P. Good Times' presentation to portfolio founders, October 2008

factChecks.note: Circuit City가 2008년 당시 미국 2위 가전 유통업체(1위 Best Buy)였다는 점을 보도 자료로 확인하세요.
2008년 11월 10일 파산보호 신청 당시 회사가 '공급업체의 신용 조건 강화'를 원인 중 하나로 들었는지 원문 보도자료로 확인하세요. 카드에는 구체 금액 없이 정성적으로만 적었습니다.
2009년 1월 16일 청산 발표, 2009년 3월 초 전 매장 폐점, 일자리 '수만 개'(보도상 약 3만 명대) 표현을 확인하세요. 정확한 매장 수·인원은 카드에 넣지 않았습니다.
2007년 숙련 판매직 수천 명(보도상 약 3,400명)을 저임금 인력으로 교체한 일은 널리 보도됐습니다. 카드에는 'thousands'로만 적었습니다.
Lehman 파산(2008.9.15) 직후 Reserve Primary Fund의 원금 손실(breaking the buck, 9.16), 기업어음(CP) 시장 경색, Fed의 CP 매입 기구(CPFF, 2008년 10월) 순서를 Federal Reserve History로 확인하세요.
Best Buy가 위기를 넘기고 Circuit City 폐점 후 고객과 점유율을 흡수했다는 보도를 확인하세요. 구체 점유율 수치는 넣지 않았습니다.
Sequoia의 'R.I.P. Good Times' 발표(2008년 10월)가 투자 기업에 비용 절감과 현금 확보를 권고했다는 내용을 확인하세요.
파견 회사 사례는 전부 가상이며 수치를 쓰지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Circuit City in 2008: the shop that ran out of credit before it ran out of customers
body: In autumn 2008, Circuit City was one of America's biggest electronics chains, second only to Best Buy.
By March 2009, every store had closed. Customers were buying less, but that is not what finished it first.

image.label: An electronics store with full shelves and a closing-down banner
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 대형 가전 매장 외관, 진열대엔 TV가 가득한데 출입문 위에 'Closing' 현수막. 실제 Circuit City 로고·상표·빨간 플러그 마크는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Which threat could close you fastest?
body: You run a large electronics chain. Sales are falling and you are losing money. Like most retailers, you stock TVs and laptops now and pay suppliers weeks later.
The holidays are coming. Lehman Brothers has just collapsed, and every lender is nervous.

options.text: Customers cutting back on big purchases
options.feedback: It hurts, but slowly. Falling sales shrink profit over months; you can cut stock and costs to match.

options.text: Suppliers asking to be paid sooner, or upfront
options.feedback: This one hits cash right away. Suddenly you must pay for holiday stock before you sell it, with money you may not have.

options.text: A rival cutting prices for the holidays
options.feedback: A real squeeze on margins, but price wars play out over seasons. It rarely empties your bank account in weeks.

cards.title: The suppliers moved first.
body: On November 10, 2008, Circuit City filed for bankruptcy protection. It said suppliers had **tightened credit terms**, draining the cash it needed to stock up for the holidays.
It hoped to reorganize. But in the middle of a crisis, no buyer or lender stepped in. In January 2009 it announced it would sell off everything, and tens of thousands of jobs went with it.

cards.title: From Wall Street to the stockroom in weeks.
list: **Sept 15, 2008:** Lehman Brothers files the largest bankruptcy in US history
A big money market fund holding Lehman debt loses money, and investors rush out of similar funds
Those funds stop buying the short-term IOUs companies use to pay bills, so even healthy firms struggle to borrow
Banks and suppliers protect themselves by lending less and demanding cash sooner
cards.callout: The US central bank set up emergency programs to restart short-term lending.
cards.softwareNote: Startups felt it as a funding freeze. In October 2008, venture firm Sequoia warned its founders to cut costs and make their cash last, because the next funding round might not come.

cards.title: Credit crunch
body: A **credit crunch** is when lenders and suppliers pull back credit at the same time, so businesses must fill payment gaps with their own cash.
Almost every business runs on gaps: buy stock now, pay later; do the work now, get paid later. In good times, credit fills those gaps quietly. In a crunch, the gap becomes a bill due today.
Circuit City's problem was not one bad quarter. It was suddenly needing cash it had always borrowed.

image.label: A timeline gap between paying suppliers and getting paid, bridged by credit
image.brief: 가로 타임라인 인포그래픽. 왼쪽 'Pay supplier', 오른쪽 'Customer pays', 사이 간격을 'Credit'이라고 쓴 다리가 연결. 두 번째 그림에서 다리가 무너지고 'Your cash' 웅덩이로 메워야 하는 모습.

cards.title: Cash bought time, and then customers.
body: Rival Best Buy faced the same falling demand. But it came through the crisis and picked up many of Circuit City's former customers once the stores closed.

The pattern repeated across industries. Firms with cash and long-term funding could keep shelves full, keep good staff and even buy weaker rivals' assets cheaply. Firms living on short-term credit spent the crisis trying to survive the next payment.

cards.title: The crunch was the final blow, not the only one.
body: Circuit City was already weak. It had lost ground to Best Buy for years, and in 2007 it replaced thousands of experienced sales staff with cheaper hires. A credit crunch tends to finish businesses that are already fragile.
Cash also has a cost. Money sitting idle in normal years earns little. The aim is not maximum cash, but enough to survive if credit vanishes for a few months.

cards.title: Now it's a staffing agency.
body: You place temporary workers with corporate clients. You pay workers every week; clients pay you about two months later. A bank credit line covers the gap.
News of a banking crisis breaks. Your bank says it is "reviewing" credit lines. What do you do this week?

options.text: Draw part of the line now and ask clients to pay faster
options.feedback: You pay a little interest on cash you may not need, but you stop depending on a nervous bank's next decision.

options.text: Cut your rates to win clients from struggling rivals
options.feedback: More clients means a bigger payment gap to fund, at exactly the moment credit is shrinking.

options.text: Wait. The credit line is signed, so it's safe
options.feedback: A signed line beats a promise. But conditions in the agreement can let a bank cut it if your numbers slip.

cards.title: In a crisis, credit can disappear before customers do.
body: Know which gaps in your business are filled by someone else's money, and how long you could last if that money stopped.
**Try it today:** list who lets you pay later and who you let pay later. Add up how many weeks of bills you could cover with cash alone.
